recipe.title: Simmered Pork and Potatoes
recipe.subtitle: A weeknight one-pot simmer: pork, potatoes, carrot and onion cooked down in a sweet-savory broth until the potatoes fall apart at the edges.
recipe.source_label: Original recipe and cooking video by Shojikudo Kitchen (in Japanese).
recipe.shopping_note: Most of this list is ordinary supermarket shopping. The two exceptions are mirin and dashi granules, which live in the East Asian aisle of a large supermarket or in any Japanese, Korean or Chinese grocery. Both keep for months, so buy them once.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder, thinly sliced
ingredients.note: Sold pre-sliced at East Asian groceries as "shabu-shabu" pork. Otherwise ask the butcher to slice it thin, or freeze a piece for 30 minutes and slice it yourself.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: Use a floury variety — Russet or Maris Piper. Waxy potatoes stay firm and will not soak up the broth.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.note: Japanese-style soy sauce. Chinese light soy is saltier — start with 1.5 tbsp and taste.

ingredients.name: Cooking sake
ingredients.note: Dry sherry works. Do not use "cooking sake" that lists added salt without cutting the soy sauce back.

ingredients.name: Mirin
ingredients.note: If you cannot find it, use 2 tbsp water plus 2 tsp sugar and add it with the soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Dashi granules
ingredients.note: Instant dashi powder. Substitute 200 ml of light chicken or vegetable stock in place of the water.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: Light brown sugar suits this better than white.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and cut out any eyes. Peel the carrot and trim off the leafy end. Trim the root end off the onion and peel it.
steps.note: Leaving the root end on the onion until after you cut it keeps the wedges held together in the pot.

steps.text: Cut the potatoes and carrot into rolling wedges. Cut the onion into wedges about 1 cm thick.
steps.note: A rolling wedge cut: slice diagonally, roll the vegetable a quarter turn toward you, slice again. Every piece ends up with more cut surface than a plain cube, which is how the broth gets inside in only 20 minutes.

steps.text: Cut the sliced pork into bite-sized pieces.
steps.note: Bite-sized here means one chopstick-load — roughly 4 cm across.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork until it is no longer pink. Add the onion, carrot and potatoes and cook, stirring, until the surfaces turn translucent.
steps.note: You are not browning anything here. Stop as soon as the potato edges go glassy — colour would make the broth muddy.

steps.text: Add the water, soy sauce, sake, mirin, dashi granules and sugar. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam that rises.
steps.note: The foam is protein from the pork. Skimming it is what keeps the finished broth clear rather than cloudy.

steps.text: Lower the heat, cover the surface with a drop lid and simmer for about 20 minutes, until a skewer goes through the potatoes without resistance.
steps.note: A drop lid sits directly on the food instead of on the pot rim, so a shallow amount of broth circulates over everything without you stirring and breaking the potatoes. Cut a circle of parchment slightly smaller than the pot and pierce a hole in the middle.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and let it stand for 10 minutes before serving.
steps.note: This rest is where most of the flavour arrives. The broth is drawn back into the potatoes as everything cools, so do not skip it.
